sections.section_title: Software control of two external memories
sections.text_helper: Section 19.4.21 "Software control of two external memories" in chapter 19 (Extended-SPI interface (XSPI)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 524.
sections.section_content:
One XSPI instance is able to control the generation of the two chip-select signals
(NCS1andNCS2). This allows two external memories to be connected to the same I/O port
driven by the XSPI.
The XSPI generates one NCS signal and the user defines how the NCS is directed to NCS1
or NCS2, by setting the CSSEL bit in XSPI_CR. Intended operation is semistatic
commutation, such as starting an application reading an external flash memory and then, for
the rest of the application, use an external SRAM connected to the same I/O bus.
From a memory-map point of view, these two memories are located in the same address
range.
